Although existing robust AEP literature addresses uncertain renewable outputs, it often overlooks the variability of ultimate load demand; consequently, no current models combine robust planning with simultaneous hedging against load fluctuations and uncertain generation. This study introduces a novel robust multi-area expansion planning framework that models uncertainty using an adaptive ambiguity set defined by bounded set variables. Specifically, load parameters are represented as polytopic sets, while renewable generation is characterized as an ellipsopic set. By formulating a distribution-free robust optimization approach based on these uncertainty structures, we establish mathematically minimal yet sufficient worst-case costs. An efficient computational algorithm, which relies solely on solving a finite sequence of deterministic second-order cone programs (SOCPs), is developed. To validate the proposed framework, comparative simulations are conducted against other optimal and robust planning strategies. The numerical analysis confirms the method's superiority in handling uncertainty and demonstrates its ability to mitigate costs associated with worst-case power outages effectively.

Due to the inherent cross-orbital angular momentum (COAM) coupling in conventional single-mode fibers (SMF), adjacent OAM modes cross-talk, restricting transmission distances. To address this, we propose a novel single-mode fiber (SMF) architecture incorporating a long-haul OAM channel. Our design features an elliptical core with periodic, rectangular index variations arranged along a full-circle path relative to the center. By strategically altering the aspect ratio of the rectangular indents, we create an effective refractive index profile that supports distinct OAM pathways while preserving single-mode operation. Specifically, a rectangular structure with lower indices on two sides and higher indices on the other causes light to traverse primarily along the wider dimension; conversely, its oval counterpart guides light along the narrower dimension.
